surcharge = an extra amount added to a price for a particular reason
handling fee = a small extra charge for processing an order or payment
postage and packing = the extra you pay for wrapping and sending goods
cashback = money returned as a reward, or extra cash taken at a shop till
online banking = managing your bank account through a website
mobile banking = managing your bank account on a smartphone app
credit rating = a judgement of how likely you are to repay borrowed money
card fraud = crime that uses stolen card details to buy goods or take money
withdraw cash = to take money out of a bank account as notes
bank balance = the amount of money in an account at a given time
overspend = to spend more money than you planned or can afford
keep to a budget = to spend only the amount of money you have planned
disposable income = money left after tax and essential bills, for spending or saving
go bust = to fail financially and close a business (informal)
creditworthy = judged likely to repay a loan on time
haggle = to argue about the price in order to pay less
extortionate = far too expensive; unreasonably high in price
guarantee = a promise to repair or replace goods if they fail within a period
live on a shoestring = to live on very little money
tighten one's belt = to spend less because money is short
